title: prioritize-kernel-pinning-kv-prefetch-and-microbatching-to-cut-streaming-tail-latency
author: Diego Morales
description: Context: Streaming endpoints intermittently show long tail latency when many small realtime requests interleave with longer context generations. Root causes observed in perf lab: (1) scheduler unfairness that allowed long-running token loops to hold kernels for multiple micro-batches, (2) KV cache misses at first map-access for recently hot prefixes, and (3) flush cadence that was optimized for throughput not tail latency. Goal: reduce p95/p99 token emission latency for single-token and low-length streams without regressing throughput for bulk workloads. Summary of changes: 1) Scheduler: added a lightweight per-worker priority bucket and a short-lived kernel pin (100-300ms) for streaming lanes so that in-progress streaming requests get priority on the active compute slice. This is implemented in scheduler/slice_scheduler.cpp with minimal state and a new metric scheduler_streaming_preemptions. 2) KV cache prefetch: introduced heuristic-based soft prefetch for likely next-key accesses for streaming requests. The runtime now probes kv_cache asynchronously on token generation hot-paths and fills a fastmap before the kernel executes (runtime/kv_prefetch.{hh,cc}). Prefetch is gated behind a runtime flag (--streaming-prefetch=on) and respects memory pressure. 3) Microbatch flush cadence: replaced fixed flush intervals with a latency-first adaptive flush policy that dynamically reduces flush windows to favor low token-latency under observed tail events. Implemented in batching/flush_policy.cpp; default remains throughput-friendly but will transiently reduce to 1-3ms for streaming-critical lanes. 4) Kernel selection hint: added a lightweight hint to the kernel selection path to favor lower-latency kernels for streaming lanes, skipping heavier fused kernels that increase single-token latency. This is a heuristic, not a hard override, so it does not change results, only kernel choice. 5) Observability: new metrics streaming_tail_latency_p95, streaming_kv_prefetch_hit, scheduler_streaming_preemptions and dashboard panels. Tests and validation: - Microbench harness: new microbench stories added to benchmark-lab that mimic interleaved streaming+batch workloads. - End-to-end smoke tests: streaming throughput and correctness retained; no API surface changes. - Perf results: p95 reduced by ~28% and p99 by ~19% across lab workloads with <2% throughput loss on bulk workloads. Implementation notes: commits break changes into focused logical units so reviewers can gate each piece. Prefetch path uses lock-free queues and backpressure tokens to avoid memory amplification. The kernel-hint path is an annotation only accepted by compatible kernels. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag; enabled by default on streaming-optimized clusters after a staged rollout with canary traffic. Related work: complements earlier backpressure improvements (see ENG-9120) and streaming flush cadence experiments (ENG-9402).
commits_summary: 9 commits: 1) add scheduler streaming priority and preemption counters; 2) implement kv prefetch async path and unit tests; 3) adaptive flush policy with config knobs; 4) kernel hint plumbing and tests; 5) metrics and dashboards; 6) microbench stories; 7) integration test tweaks; 8) docs/console notes; 9) small fix to prefetch memory accounting.
review_comments: Arielle Hu: Requested that prefetch be gated by an additional LRU threshold to avoid warming cold prefixes. Diego: Added LRU gating and updated tests to simulate memory pressure. Sven Petrov: Asked for more conservative default pin duration; reduced from 500ms to 100-300ms adaptive window. Maya Kapoor: Noted potential regression on multi-tenant Dedicated pools; added rollout gating and a cluster-level toggle. CI initially: pipeline failed on lint for missing header include in kv_prefetch.hh; fixed in commit 6 and retriggered. Performance CI: first perf nanobench run showed a small regression on a 4k-token bulk synthetic; we limited kernel hint to streaming lanes only and re-ran. Final CI: all checks passed including unit, integration, lint, and perf. Review outcome: approvers Arielle Hu and Sven Petrov approved after two iteration cycles; Maya approved conditionally and re-verified on canary. Merge details: merged via squash, merge_commit_sha: "a1f3b9c6e2d4f8b7"; merge method: "squash".
release_notes: Reduced streaming token tail latency via scheduler priority, kv prefetch, and adaptive microbatch flush cadence. p95/p99 improvements for interleaved streaming workloads. Flag: --streaming-prefetch (default on for streaming clusters).
